title: Council Extends Ukraine Territorial Integrity Sanctions Listings for Three Years, Ending Six-Month Renewal Cycle
detail: The Council of the EU prolonged its individual sanctions listings targeting those responsible for undermining or threatening Ukraine's territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence for 36 months, until 22 September 2029 — a break from the previous practice of renewing the listings every six months. The measures cover more than 3,000 individuals and entities and include travel bans, asset freezes and a prohibition on making funds available to those listed. As part of the periodic review, the Council declined to renew the listings of three individuals and one entity and removed three deceased persons from the list.

title: General Affairs Council Debates 2028–2034 EU Budget, Members Split on New 'Own Resources'
detail: EU affairs ministers held a policy debate at the General Affairs Council on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (2028–2034) and began preparing the agenda for the October European Council. Member states largely held their existing positions: Germany said it remained open to new EU 'own resources' except a proposed tax on large companies, while Denmark and Germany cautioned that new revenue streams were not a 'magic solution' to budget pressures. Deeper divisions persist between Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands, who want a leaner budget focused on competitiveness, defence and migration, and France, Poland and Italy, who want to preserve historical agricultural and cohesion spending. The Irish Council Presidency aims to table its own compromise text in the first week of October, with the goal of a political agreement among the 27 by the end of 2026 so funding is not interrupted from January 2028.
